result.title: Faces or Models? Where the Age Gap in Facial Expression Recognition Comes From
result.summary: Facial expression recognition (FER) systems are increasingly used in elder care, yet their accuracy on older faces is rarely measured. This study evaluated five open-source FER models on the FACES database, which holds 2,052 posed photographs of 171 adults aged 19 to 80. The models cross three architectures (ResNet-18, POSTER++ and QCS) with two training datasets (RAF-DB and AffectNet). All models lost accuracy on older faces by 11.7 to 15.2 percentage points. Older faces were harder for people too: human raters lost 8.6 points, a classifier using only facial geometry lost 8.3, and for anger, fear, and happiness older adults differed more from one another when posing. On specific expressions the models fell much further than people did. AffectNet-trained models misread older neutral faces as sad or angry 62% of the time. RAF-DB-trained models lost fear, disgust, and anger instead. The gap persisted after controlling for architecture, image quality, cropping, and expression intensity. When only the final classification layer was refitted on older faces, the gap shrank from 11 to 21 points to 4 points or less, suggesting that the models' learned features can represent older faces and that the deficit lies in how the final layer was trained.

AI.brief_summary: 该研究在 FACES 数据库上评测五个开源 FER 模型，量化其对老年面孔的准确率下降，并通过仅重训最后一层分类头来定位这一差距的来源。
AI.relevance_reason: 重训最后的分类层即可把年龄差距压到 4 点以内，提示缺陷不在表示而在分类头训练，这一「表示可保留但未被使用」的诊断思路可供核查 LVR 中潜变量内容是否被答案真正使用的评估方法。
